verdict: Instant for your own workspace. Distributing to other workspaces is mostly self-serve. Listing in the Slack Marketplace is the slow part: the longest review queue of the four.
start_now: If you need a Marketplace listing at launch, submit as early as possible. A rejected or broken submission resets your place in the queue.

cases.outcome: Works as soon as you install it to your own workspace
Turn on public distribution; no Marketplace review
Preliminary review (up to 10 business days) + functional review (up to 10 weeks)

blockers.text: Once listed, scopes and config are locked. Each later change goes through review again, up to 6 weeks.
In the preliminary review, every resubmission resets your place in the queue. Once a reviewer is assigned in the functional review, resubmitting keeps it.
Reviewers need a working test account on your product, not just Slack.
Some scopes are not accepted in the Marketplace at all.
Don't request scopes for features you haven't built yet; Slack rejects them. Legacy and broad scopes (identity.*, admin.*) aren't accepted, and coded workflows can't be listed at all.

sources.t: WorkOS: OAuth app approval on Slack, Microsoft, Atlassian

facts.q: Do you need a paid plan to create the OAuth app, or for any feature the agent needs (e.g. webhooks)?
facts.a: Not documented in the pages read. Creating a Slack app needs a Slack account and a workspace to install it in.

facts.q: Is there a sandbox or test environment, or do you test against a real account?
facts.a: Test in your own workspace. Marketplace reviewers can't use your workspaces, so they need a way to install the app themselves plus test credentials for your product.

facts.q: Is there any review, approval or user cap before other people's accounts can connect?
facts.a: A Marketplace listing needs a preliminary review (up to 10 business days) and a functional review (up to 10 weeks).

facts.q: Which scopes cover what the agent must do, and does any of them trigger a review?
facts.a: Depends on what the agent does; request only scopes for features that exist. Marketplace rejects legacy and broad scopes such as identity.*, admin.*, workflow.steps:execute and triggers:*.

facts.q: What redirect URL goes in when using Composio, and is localhost allowed while building?
facts.a: Use Composio's callback, https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Composio's dashboard shows the exact redirect URI for your auth config.

facts.q: How long do access tokens last, and how are they refreshed?
facts.a: Without token rotation, access tokens never expire. With rotation they expire every 12 hours and are refreshed with oauth.v2.access (grant_type=refresh_token); rotation can't be turned off once enabled.

facts.q: Whose name do users see on the consent screen?
facts.a: With Composio's managed app: "Composio wants to access your account". With your own OAuth app: your app's name.

facts.q: If you switch from Composio's managed app to your own, do users have to reconnect?
facts.a: Not documented by Composio. Each toolkit has its own auth config; plan for users to reconnect, since tokens belong to the OAuth app that issued them.
